2026 SHENZHEN INTERNATIONAL FINTECH COMPETITION | INTERNATIONAL TRACK | TOPIC F
NULL Wallet
The AI wallet that must reject “no edge” before it moves money
H0H_0: no net edge after costs  →  reject with evidence, or refuse and record the refusal
Theme: AI as a Financial Participant
Team: AskWallet  |  Brandon Haris Effendi (team leader, MSc Finance), Maulik Bansal (MSc Finance), Desylionie Onggani Winata (MSc Logistics Management), Lund University, Sweden  |  br5880ha-s@student.lu.se
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
AI agents with wallets need proof, not just permission: NULL Wallet moves money only after rejecting “no edge”
The gap
Spend limits and allowlists ask is this transfer permitted? Nobody asks is the reason real? An agent can obey every limit and still trade on noise.
Our answer
A wallet that must reject H0H_0 (no net edge after costs) with pre-registered, multiplicity-corrected tests before value moves. Every refusal is a hash-chained, on-chain-anchored record.
Result
Strict where nothing exists to find, sensitive where something does, and honest about both.
0.0%
false GO in 1,000 no-edge simulated markets
92%
GO when a moderate edge truly exists
0 of 36
monthly verdicts on real BTC allowed trading
-20%
wallet loss of the same models run without the court
So what: evidence before permission makes an AI agent’s wallet auditable, and refusing to trade becomes a result you can prove.
Source: Team analysis; Monte Carlo of 1,000 simulated markets; replay of real BTC hourly data 2019-12-18 to 2022-11-14 (sandbox, assumed costs)NULL Wallet  |  2
PROBLEM
Six families of causes make agents trade on false edges, and each one has a control in NULL Wallet
So what: most losses come from acting on a pattern that was never real; the controls act on the reason, not only on the transfer.
Source: Team root-cause analysis (fishbone); controls map to code modules in the repositoryNULL Wallet  |  3
SOLUTION
Two separated pipes decide whether to act and how to act, and meet only at the latest GO receipt
at=𝟙[GOtfresh]⋅𝟙[π(it)=allow]a_t=\mathbb{1}\left[\mathrm{GO}_{t}^{\,\mathrm{fresh}}\right]\cdot\mathbb{1}\left[\pi(i_t)=\mathrm{allow}\right]
Evidence pipe
Decides whether the strategy deserves capital.
Action pipe
Decides whether this move is allowed. Plain code, no model.
Ledger
Hash-chained; head anchored on-chain.
So what: a compromised or confused language layer still cannot sign anything the policy engine π\pi does not approve.

SECURITY
Pre-registration and a hash chain make every decision, and every refusal, tamper-evident
h0=SHA256(canon(𝒫))(protocol committed before data)h_0=\mathrm{SHA256}\!\left(\mathrm{canon}(\mathcal{P})\right)\quad\text{(protocol committed before data)}
ht=SHA256(ht−1‖canon(et))h_t=\mathrm{SHA256}\!\left(h_{t-1}\,\Vert\,\mathrm{canon}(e_t)\right)
calldata=𝙽𝚄𝙻𝙻𝟷‖ht⇒0-value self-transaction\mathrm{calldata}=\texttt{NULL1}\,\Vert\,h_t\quad\Rightarrow\quad\text{0-value self-transaction}
Why it matters
Edit, delete or reorder any entry and every later hash changes. Anchoring hth_t on-chain stops the tail from being cut silently.
So what: the record of why the wallet acted, or refused, cannot be rewritten after the fact.
Source: nullwallet/ledger.py; nullwallet/onchain.py; tests/test_redteam.py (LedgerTamper)NULL Wallet  |  6

Isolated signer
Key only in an environment variable; never in logs or receipts.
Strict intent schema
Unknown fields are rejected; look-alike addresses fail.

So what: strict where there is nothing to find, sensitive where there is something, with the trade-off shown openly.

EVIDENCE 2: REAL DATA
The models do beat a naive forecast, but their edge never reaches twice the cost: a result we reproduced
c=7.54bpc=7.54\ \mathrm{bp} per switch (fee, slippage, square-root impact, gas)
GO⇔G0..G5pass,c*≥2c\mathrm{GO}\iff \mathrm{G0..G5\ pass},\quad c^{*}\ge 2c
Funnel (36 windows)
93 of 180 candidate tests show skill; none pass the net-edge gate or the cost margin.
WATCH is a result
The pattern is statistically there but not tradable, so the wallet stays in reserve.
So what: statistical skill ≠\neq economic edge: the break-even cost c*c^{*} is the number that decides.
Source: Court receipts on real BTC; modelled cost 7.54 bp per switch, 2x margin requiredNULL Wallet  |  11
EVIDENCE 3: HONEST LIMITS
Stress-testing exposed a weakness that we fixed and disclose: a GO is evidence about the past, not a guarantee
Cost sweep
GO in 8 to 10 of 36 windows at zero cost (two machines), 1 at 0.25c0.25c, none at 0.5c0.5c or above.
A failure we found
The zero-cost run lost money in the March 2020 crash.
σ̂24>3σ̂W⇒st=0\hat\sigma_{24}>3\,\hat\sigma_{W}\ \Rightarrow\ s_t=0 (regime guard)
Disclosure
The guard was added after the fact, so we claim no out-of-sample benefit.
So what: caps, kill-switch and guard are essential; the honesty of the receipt is the product.
Source: Cost sweep on real BTC; regime guard added after the first replay (post hoc)NULL Wallet  |  12
INNOVATION
What is new: evidence before permission, pre-registered and attested, with refusals as first-class records
1. Court gates
Classical econometrics as a permission layer.
2. Data-snooping control
Holm over every candidate tried.
3. Pre-registration
Protocol hashed before the data is examined.
4. Attested refusals
Every HOLD and WATCH is a receipt, anchored on-chain.
5. Language never reaches the key
Typed intents and a deterministic gate.
So what: the standard tests are old; putting them in front of an agent’s key, with proof of refusal, is the new part.
Source: Public descriptions of agent-wallet products and arXiv 2601.04583 (survey); positioning is our qualitative judgementNULL Wallet  |  13

Costs and multiple testingNet-of-cost edge, break-even cost, data snooping, neutral zone, HOLD/WATCHG4 net edge; G5 cost margin; Holm over candidates; dead-band; verdicts
